title: The Verb: The Past
summary: The past places an event before now, and covers what English splits into a simple past and a perfect. Its marker is -ఏ- (or -ఇన్- before -ది), with a small class of verbs that take -నా- instead — and the personal endings of ¶74 close the form as they do in every other tense.

rules.heading: How Telugu Divides Time
rules.statement: Telugu finite verbs mark **three** tense-modes a learner meets first: the **progressive** in -తు- + ఉండు (¶76), the **habitual/future** in -తా- (¶78), and the **past** treated in this section. English’s continuous, simple, and perfect are not a matching three-way split in Telugu.

examples.gloss: I am reading. (progressive — action going on now)
I read (habitually); or, I will read.

footnotes: A continuous or perfect sense built with an auxiliary (past participle + ఉండు, and the rest of the compound system) belongs with the compound verb, not with a fourth synthetic tense.

sources.citation: Krishnamurti, Bhadriraju & Gwynn, J. P. L., *A Grammar of Modern Telugu*. Delhi: Oxford University Press, 1985.

rules.heading: The Past — ఏ / ఇన్
rules.statement: The past is formed by adding the tense suffix **-ఏ-** to the past stem, then a personal ending of ¶74. Before the non-masculine singular **-ది**, **-ఏ-** is replaced by **-ఇన్-**: *వెళ్ళింది*, not *వెళ్ళాది*.

paradigms.caption: వెళ్ళు — past
paradigms.footnote: The past of Telugu answers both English *went* and *have gone* (K&G §15.2).

examples.gloss: Yesterday he went to the village.
She read / has read the book.

sources.citation: Krishnamurti, Bhadriraju & Gwynn, J. P. L., *A Grammar of Modern Telugu*. Delhi: Oxford University Press, 1985.
Wikipedia contributors, “Telugu grammar.” Wikipedia, The Free Encyclopedia.
sources.note: Paradigm of వెళ్ళు in the past.

rules.heading: The Past Stem
rules.statement: A stem-final **-ు** is dropped before the past suffix. A non-initial medial **-ు-** of the root becomes **-ి-**: *చదువు* → *చదివాను*, *అడుగు* → *అడిగాను*.

sources.citation: Krishnamurti, Bhadriraju & Gwynn, J. P. L., *A Grammar of Modern Telugu*. Delhi: Oxford University Press, 1985.
Wiktionary contributors, “Appendix:Telugu verbs.” Wiktionary, The Free Dictionary.

rules.heading: The -నా- Class
rules.statement: After a stem ending in a short vowel + **-న్**, the past suffix is **-నా-** (and **-న-** before **-ది**), with the final consonant doubled: *తిను* → *తిన్నాను*, *తిన్నది*. The class is small — అను, తిను, విను, కొను, కను, ఉండు, కూర్చొను, నిల్చును, and a few others.

sources.citation: Krishnamurti, Bhadriraju & Gwynn, J. P. L., *A Grammar of Modern Telugu*. Delhi: Oxford University Press, 1985.
Wiktionary contributors, “Appendix:Telugu verbs.” Wiktionary, The Free Dictionary.

rules.heading: పడు — -డా-
rules.statement: After the stem **పడ్**, the past suffix is **-డా-** (and **-డ-** before **-ది**): *పడ్డాను*, *పడ్డది* / *పడింది*.

sources.citation: Krishnamurti, Bhadriraju & Gwynn, J. P. L., *A Grammar of Modern Telugu*. Delhi: Oxford University Press, 1985.

rules.heading: Denying the Past — again
rules.statement: The past is denied by the **infinitive stem + లేదు**, one form for every person (¶81): *వెళ్ళలేదు*, *తినలేదు*, *చేయలేదు*. The affirmative’s person ending disappears; the negative tense of ¶82 is not used here.

examples.target: నిన్న నేను వెళ్ళాను. → నిన్న నేను వెళ్ళలేదు.
examples.gloss: Yesterday I went. → Yesterday I did not go.
examples.roman: ninna nēnu veḷḷānu. → ninna nēnu veḷḷalēdu.

examples.gloss: She ate. → She did not eat.

sources.citation: Krishnamurti, Bhadriraju & Gwynn, J. P. L., *A Grammar of Modern Telugu*. Delhi: Oxford University Press, 1985.

rules.heading: చేయు and Noun + చేయు
rules.statement: **చేయు** *to do* takes a past stem **చేస్- / చేశ్-**: *చేశాను*, *చేశాడు*, *చేసింది*. After a noun it is a verbaliser — *పని చేయు* *to work*, *వంట చేయు* *to cook* — and only **చేయు** conjugates; the noun is unchanged.

examples.gloss: He did not do this work.

footnotes: పనిచేయు as one orthographic word and పని చేయు as two are the same construction: the tense and person endings attach to చేయు alone, never to పని.

sources.citation: Krishnamurti, Bhadriraju & Gwynn, J. P. L., *A Grammar of Modern Telugu*. Delhi: Oxford University Press, 1985.
sources.note: Examples with pani cees- and cees- throughout §15–§16.
Verbaliser after a noun or adjective; Brown (1903) cited there.

vocabulary.gloss: to do; verbaliser after a noun

drills.stem: Which Telugu form covers both English *I went* and *I have gone*?
drills.explanation: The past వెళ్ళాను answers both English past and perfect (¶96–¶97). వెళ్తాను is habitual/future; వెళ్ళుతున్నాను is progressive; వెళ్ళలేదు denies the past.

drills.stem: **ఆమె వెళ్ళింది** — which tense suffix stands before **-ది**?
drills.explanation: Before non-masculine -ది the past uses -ఇన్-, giving వెళ్ళింది. -ఏ- appears everywhere else in the ordinary past; -నా- belongs to the తిను class; -తా- is habitual/future.

drills.stem: What is the past of **చదువు** for **నేను**?
drills.explanation: Medial -ు- becomes -ి- before the past suffix: చదువు → చదివాను (¶98). చదువుతాను is habitual/future; చదవను is the negative tense; చదువుతున్నాను is progressive.

drills.stem: **మాధవ్ నిన్న ఆపిల్ ______.** Which form fills the blank?
drills.explanation: నిన్న puts the eating in the past; తిను belongs to the -నా- class, so అతను / మాధవ్ takes తిన్నాడు (¶99). తింటాడు is habitual/future; తింటున్నాడు progressive; తినడు the negative tense.

drills.stem: **మాధవ్ నిన్న ఆపిల్ తిన్నాడు, కానీ ఈ రోజు ఆరెంజ్ ______.**
drills.explanation: Yesterday’s past is already given; ఈ రోజు with an action going on now takes the progressive తింటున్నాడు (¶76, ¶96). A second తిన్నాడు would keep both clauses in the past; తినలేదు denies the past; తిన్నది is non-masculine.

drills.stem: Which is the past of **పడు** for **అతను**?
drills.explanation: పడు takes -డా- in the past: పడ్డాడు (¶100). పడతాడు is habitual/future; పడతున్నాడు progressive; పడలేదు denies the past.

drills.stem: **నిన్న నేను పని చేశాను.** Which part of the phrase carries the past ending?
options: neither — the past is in నిన్న
drills.explanation: పని is the noun; చేయు is the verbaliser and alone takes చేశాను (¶102). Writing పనిచేశాను as one word does not move the ending onto పని.
Past denial is infinitive + లేదు: తినలేదు (¶101). తినదు is the negative tense (habitual/future); తినటం లేదు denies the progressive; కాదు denies identity, not an action.
చదివాను and అడిగాడు show the ordinary past with medial -ి-; తిన్నది is the -నా- class past. చదువుతాను is habitual/future (-తా-).

drills.stem: Which statements about **పని చేయు** are correct?
options: Only చేయు takes the tense and person endings.
పని must always be written solid with చేయు as పనిచేయు.
పని చేశాను and పనిచేశాను are the same construction.
The past of పని చేయు for ఆమె is పని చేసింది.
drills.explanation: The noun may be spaced or closed; morphology is unchanged. చేసింది is the non-masculine past of చేయు. Nothing forces the solid spelling.

drills.stem: Among **వెళ్ళాను, వెళ్తాను, వెళ్ళుతున్నాను, వెళ్ళలేదు, చదివింది**, how many forms are in the **past affirmative**?
drills.explanation: Two: వెళ్ళాను and చదివింది. వెళ్తాను is habitual/future; వెళ్ళుతున్నాను progressive; వెళ్ళలేదు is past *negative*, not the affirmative past.

drills.stem: Among **తిన్నాను, విన్నది, కొన్నాడు, పడ్డాడు, అన్నాను**, how many take the special past suffix **-నా-** (not -ఏ- or -డా-)?
drills.explanation: Four: తిన్నాను, విన్నది, కొన్నాడు, అన్నాను belong to the -నా- class (¶99). పడ్డాడు is the separate -డా- pattern of పడు (¶100).

drills.stem: Which form is the **odd one out** by tense?
drills.explanation: The first three are past. వెళ్తారు is habitual/future (-తా-), with the geminate of వెళ్ళు simplified.

drills.stem: Match each form to the system that produces it.
drills.explanation: చదివాను is past; చదువుతాను habitual/future; చదువుతున్నాను progressive; చదవలేదు past negation with లేదు.

drills.title: నిన్న
drills.passage: నిన్న మాధవ్ ఇంట్లో లేడు. అతను ఊరికి వెళ్ళాడు. అక్కడ అన్నం తిన్నాడు, కానీ ఆపిల్ తినలేదు. అమ్మ వంట చేసింది. నేను పుస్తకం చదివాను. ఈ రోజు మాధవ్ ఇక్కడ ఉన్నాడు — ఇప్పుడు పని చేస్తున్నాడు.
drills.translation: Yesterday Madhav was not at home. He went to the village. There he ate rice, but he did not eat an apple. Mother cooked. I read a book. Today Madhav is here — he is working now.

questions.explanation: The passage says అతను ఊరికి వెళ్ళాడు.
The passage says అన్నం తిన్నాడు, కానీ ఆపిల్ తినలేదు — rice yes, apple no.

questions.stem: Which verbs in the passage are in the **past affirmative**?
questions.explanation: వెళ్ళాడు, తిన్నాడు, and చేసింది (in వంట చేసింది) are past. చేస్తున్నాడు is progressive — today’s work, not yesterday’s.

questions.stem: In the passage, how many **distinct past-affirmative verb forms** appear (count each written verb once)?
questions.explanation: Four: వెళ్ళాడు, తిన్నాడు, చేసింది, చదివాను. తినలేదు is past *negative*; చేస్తున్నాడు is progressive; లేడు and ఉన్నాడు are forms of ఉండు / లే-, not the past affirmative of an action verb in this count.

drills.romanization: ninna mādhav iṇṭlō lēḍu. atanu ūriki veḷḷāḍu. akkaḍa annaṁ tinnāḍu, kānī āpil tinalēdu. amma vaṇṭa cēsindi. nēnu pustakaṁ cadivānu. ī rōju mādhav ikkaḍa unnāḍu — ippuḍu pani cēstunnāḍu.
